definition_zh: 预后；病情预测；对事态的预测；预先知悉
definition_en: a judgment about the likely course and outcome of a disease, or a prediction of how a situation will develop
core_image: 医生站在病床边，用手指沿一条向前延伸的线，画出病情接下来要走的方向
scene: 查房时，主治医生把家属叫到走廊尽头，摊开检查报告。The doctor explained the prognosis in plain words and warned that recovery would take months.
sceneCN: 这里 prognosis 是「病情预后」（第 1 个义项：对疾病走向与结果的判断）；句意为医生用平实的话说明预后，并提醒康复需要数月。

pos.zh: 名词：预后；病情预测；预判

collocations.zh: 对康复前景的预后判断

derivatives.zh: 由本词换形容词后缀 -tic 构成，义为「预后的；预示的」
由 prognostic 加动词后缀构成，义为「凭征象预测；预言」
由 prognosticate 加 -ion 构成，义为「预测；预言」
由 prognosticate 加 -or 构成，义为「预测者；预言者」

senses.title: The expected course of a disease
senses.definition: a medical judgment about the likely course and outcome of an illness, including the chance of recovery
senses.definitionCN: 对疾病可能的发展过程与结果所作的医学判断，包括康复的可能性
senses.example: The scan showed that the prognosis for the patient was now much better.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示，这位病人的预后现在好了很多。
senses.why: Greek pro- means before and gnosis means knowing, so a prognosis is the doctor knowing the shape of the illness before it unfolds.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 pro- 意为「在前」，gnosis 意为「知」，所以 prognosis 就是医生在病情展开之前先知道它的走向。

senses.title: A prediction about future events
senses.definition: a reasoned prediction about how a situation, market, or plan is likely to develop
senses.definitionCN: 对局势、市场或计划可能如何发展的有理据的预测
senses.example: The report offered a bleak prognosis for the coming year.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对来年作出了黯淡的预测。
senses.why: Once the medical judgment is abstracted from the body, any future course can be read in advance from present signs.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把医学判断从身体上抽象出来，任何事情的未来走向都可以从当下的征象提前读出。

senses.title: The act of reading signs
senses.definition: the act of forming such a judgment by interpreting present signs, tests, or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 通过解读当下的征象、检查或证据而形成这种判断的行为
senses.example: Careful prognosis depends on repeated tests rather than on a single scan.
senses.exampleCN: 谨慎的预判依赖反复检查，而不是一次扫描。
senses.why: The word names not only the answer but the work of reading the signs that produce it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不只指答案，也指读出征象、得出答案的那番功夫。

senses.title: Foreknowledge
senses.definition: knowledge of an event before it happens, the older and more general sense of the Greek word
senses.definitionCN: 事件发生之前就已知道，这是该希腊词更早、更宽泛的含义
senses.example: In its Greek sense, prognosis simply meant foreknowledge of what was to come.
senses.exampleCN: 在其希腊语含义中，prognosis 只表示对将来之事的预先知悉。
senses.why: The root gnosis is knowing itself, so the word can name any knowing ahead of time, with or without medicine.
senses.whyCN: 词根 gnosis 就是「知」本身，所以这个词可以指任何提前的知悉，与医药有没有关系都可以。

intro.en: Prognosis joins a Greek prefix meaning before to a Greek noun meaning knowing; medicine adopted the pair for the course of an illness.
intro.cn: prognosis 由表示「在前」的希腊语前缀与表示「知」的希腊语名词合成；医学用它来说病情的走向。

items.en: Pro- means before or in front of, and it marks whatever comes earlier in time.
items.cn: pro- 意为「在前、在……之前」，标记时间上更早的一方。

items.en: Gnosis means knowing or knowledge, from the verb gignoskein, to know or recognize.
items.cn: gnosis 意为「知、知识」，出自动词 gignoskein「知道、认出」。

items.en: Prognosis was formed as a noun for knowing beforehand, and it could also mean the foretelling of an outcome.
items.cn: prognosis 作为名词表示「预先知道」，也可指对结果的预先告知。

items.en: Medical Latin adopted the Greek word for the forecast a physician makes about a disease.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语借 prognosis 表示医生对疾病的预判，这一用法在古典医学著述中已有记录。

items.en: English medical writing adopted the word in the seventeenth century, and it kept the clinical sense at its centre.
items.cn: 英语医学文献在十七世纪采用这个词，并始终以临床含义为中心。

items.en: Modern use extends the word to economics, politics and sport, where any forecast may be called a prognosis.
items.cn: 现代用法把它扩展到经济、政治与体育，任何预判都可以叫 prognosis。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Greek root gnosis, while the near-meaning group gathers words for forecasts of different strength.
note.cn: 形近组共享希腊词根 gnosis；近义组收各类预测词，把握程度各不相同。

entries.definition: An adjective for what foretells a course or outcome, and a noun for a sign of what is coming.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「预后的、预示的」；作名词指「预兆」；与本词同出希腊词根。

entries.definition: To foretell or predict, especially from signs; a formal verb built on the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「预言、预测」，多指凭征象推断，语气正式；由同一词根构成。

entries.definition: The identification of an illness from its signs, built with the prefix dia- meaning through.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「诊断」，指根据症状辨明疾病；由 dia-「穿过」加同一词根 gnosis 构成，前缀不同。

entries.definition: A statement about what is expected to happen, used for weather and general trends rather than illness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「预报、预测」，多用于天气与总体趋势，不专指病情。

entries.definition: The expected future of a situation or a patient, seen as a prospect rather than a detailed forecast.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「前景、展望」，指局势或病人的预期未来，偏重总体前景而非细致推断。

entries.definition: A statement that something will happen, the broadest and most neutral of these words.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「预言、预测」，是这组词里最宽泛、最中性的一个。

normalIntro.en: The hooks below follow the real Greek parts of the word and the phrases it keeps in medical English.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子依据这个词真实的希腊语构件，以及它在医护英语中固定的搭配。

normal.en: Pro- is before and gnosis is knowing, so prognosis is knowing before.
normal.cn: pro- 是「在前」，gnosis 是「知」，所以 prognosis 就是提前知道。

normal.en: Diagnosis and prognosis are a pair: diagnosis names the illness now, prognosis names its course later.
normal.cn: diagnosis 与 prognosis 是一对：diagnosis 说当下的病，prognosis 说往后的走向。

normal.en: A poor prognosis warns of a bad outcome, while a good prognosis leaves room for recovery.
normal.cn: a poor prognosis 提示结果不佳，a good prognosis 则留有康复余地。

normal.en: The plural is prognoses, and the final -es is pronounced as a long e.
normal.cn: 复数是 prognoses，末尾的 -es 读长音 e。

normal.en: Oncologists write the prognosis into the record so that every team reads the same outlook.
normal.cn: 肿瘤科医生把 prognosis 写进病历，让每个团队读到同样的前景判断。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor tracing a line from the bedside toward a point months ahead: the line is the prognosis.
abstract.cn: 想象医生从病床前画一条线，指向几个月后的某一点：这条线就是 prognosis。

abstract.en: The same line can be drawn for a harvest, a market or a season, because any forecast reads the future from signs.
abstract.cn: 同一条线也能画向收成、市场或季节，因为任何预测都是从征象读出未来。

abstract.en: Watch the doctor compare three test results before drawing the line: the drawing is the act of prognosis.
abstract.cn: 看医生先比对三份检查结果再画这条线：画线的过程就是 prognosis 的预判行为。

examples.en: The prognosis for a treated infection is usually excellent.
examples.cn: 经过治疗的感染，其预后通常很好。

examples.en: Analysts gave a cautious prognosis for the housing market.
examples.cn: 分析师对楼市给出了谨慎的预测。

examples.en: A second opinion confirmed the first prognosis.
examples.cn: 第二意见与最初的预后判断一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普罗格诺西斯」——把读音拆成「先摸清、再开口」：医生看准病情才说话，这就是预后与预测；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 pro-（在前）+ gnosis（知，出自 gignōskein「认识」）→ prognōsis「预先知悉」→ 医学拉丁语 prognosis「对病情走向的预判」→ 英语 prognosis。核心义是「在事情发生之前先知道」。

sensesIntro.en: Prognosis starts as a medical reading of the course of an illness, widens into any forecast of events, then narrows to the act of reading signs, and finally returns to the plain Greek sense of foreknowledge.
sensesIntro.cn: prognosis 从对疾病走向的医学判读出发，扩展到对任何事态的预测，再收窄为读征象的动作，最后回到希腊语「预先知悉」的朴素含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn from the bedside toward a point months away.
core.cn: 核心意象：从病床边画向数月之后某一点的一条线。

branches.en: MEDICINE: the line follows the illness itself, from diagnosis to outcome.
branches.cn: 医学线：这条线沿着疾病本身，从诊断走到结果。

branches.en: BEYOND THE BODY: the same line is drawn for markets, seasons and plans.
branches.cn: 身体之外：同一条线也画向市场、季节与计划。

branches.en: THE WORK: drawing the line requires tests, signs and careful reading.
branches.cn: 功夫线：画这条线需要检查、征象与仔细解读。

branches.en: THE PLAIN SENSE: knowing before anything happens, with no clinic involved.
branches.cn: 朴素义：在任何事情发生之前就知道，与诊所无关。

branches.en: Both senses promise a reading of the future, one about a body and one about the world.
branches.cn: 两个义项都承诺读出未来，一个关于身体，一个关于世事。

intro.en: Prognosis is built from a Greek prefix and a Greek noun of knowing; the same parts recur across English medical vocabulary.
intro.cn: prognosis 由希腊语前缀与表示「知」的希腊语名词构成；同样的构件也出现在英语的 diagnosis 等医学词汇里。

latinIntro.en: Greek gnosis and prognosis are recorded source forms; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed rather than attested.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 gnosis 与 prognosis 是有文献记录的来源形式；更早的印欧词根属于重构，而非实证。

items.example: The prefix places the knowing ahead of the event.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「知」放在事件之前。

items.example: Gnosis is the knowing half of the word.
items.exampleCN: gnosis 是这个词中表示「知」的那一半。

items.example: The verb is the source of the noun gnosis.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词 gnosis 的来源。

items.example: The Greek noun already meant knowing beforehand.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词本义就是「提前知道」。

items.example: English keeps the clinical sense at the centre.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它以临床含义为中心保留下来。

items.example: The adjective describes what foretells a course.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述能预示走向的东西。

items.example: The verb is formal and slightly old-fashioned.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词语气正式，略显古旧。

items.example: The suffix forms nouns of process such as prognosis.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示过程的名词，如 prognosis。

items.example: The suffix forms prognostic from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由名词构成 prognostic。

items.example: Diagnosis uses dia- through plus the same gnosis.
items.exampleCN: diagnosis 由 dia-「穿过」加同一个 gnosis 构成。

definition_en: a preparation given to a person or animal so that the body learns to resist a particular disease
core_image: 一小瓶清亮的液体，装着让身体提前演习的病原体样本
scene: 社区卫生站里，护士从冷藏箱里取出一支针剂，反复核对姓名与日期。The nurse gave the child a vaccine against measles before the family left for the city.
sceneCN: 这里 vaccine 是「疫苗」（第 1 个义项：让人体产生抵抗力的防病制剂）；句意为护士在全家进城前给孩子打了麻疹疫苗。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「给……接种疫苗」
由 vaccinate 加 -ion 构成，义为「疫苗接种；接种」
由 vaccinate 加 -or 构成，义为「接种员；接种器」
由 vaccine 加 -ology 构成，义为「疫苗学」

senses.title: A preparation that trains the immune system
senses.definition: a substance made from a weakened, killed, or partial germ that teaches the body to fight a specific disease
senses.definitionCN: 由减毒、灭活或部分病原体成分制成的物质，教身体抵抗某种特定疾病
senses.example: The measles vaccine has cut deaths among young children by a huge margin.
senses.exampleCN: 麻疹疫苗大幅降低了幼儿的死亡人数。
senses.why: The vial holds a harmless version of the germ, so the body can rehearse the fight before the real infection arrives.
senses.whyCN: 小瓶里装的是无害化的病原体，身体能在真正的感染到来之前先演习一遍。

senses.title: The germ material itself
senses.definition: the actual weakened, inactivated, or fragmentary germ material used in such a preparation, as studied in the laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 这类制剂中实际使用的减毒、灭活或片段化病原体材料，是实验室研究的对象
senses.example: The team grew the vaccine in eggs, then purified it for the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 团队用鸡蛋培养这种疫苗，再提纯用于试验。
senses.why: At the bench the word points to the material, not the shot: the germ is grown, weakened and measured.
senses.whyCN: 在实验台上，这个词指的是材料而不是那一针：病原体被培养、减毒并计量。

senses.title: The programme that delivers it
senses.definition: the organized effort of giving the preparation to a whole population, often named by the product itself
senses.definitionCN: 把这种制剂给整个人群接种的有组织行动，常直接用产品名来指代
senses.example: The vaccine reached every village in the district within six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这场疫苗接种在六周内覆盖了该地区的每个村庄。
senses.why: When millions receive the same dose, the dose becomes the name of the campaign.
senses.whyCN: 当成百万人接种同一剂时，这一剂就成了整个行动的名字。

senses.title: A safeguard against a harmful trend
senses.definition: something that protects a person or society from a harmful idea, habit, or influence, as a vaccine protects from disease
senses.definitionCN: 保护个人或社会免受有害观念、习惯或影响的事物，如同疫苗保护人免受疾病
senses.example: Plain teaching in primary school is the best vaccine against online rumor.
senses.exampleCN: 小学里的常识教育是对抗网络谣言最好的疫苗。
senses.why: The medical image travels: a small controlled dose builds resistance to a much larger threat.
senses.whyCN: 医学意象会迁移：少量可控的剂量，能对更大的威胁产生抵抗力。

intro.en: Vaccine comes from the Latin word for a cow, by way of the cowpox material that Jenner used against smallpox.
intro.cn: vaccine 来自拉丁语中表示「母牛」的词，经由詹纳用来对抗天花的牛痘材料而得名。

items.en: Vacca means cow, and the adjective vaccinus means of or from cows.
items.cn: vacca 意为「母牛」，形容词 vaccinus 意为「牛的、取自牛的」。

items.en: Physicians called cowpox variolae vaccinae, the cowpox of cows, to set it apart from smallpox.
items.cn: 医生把牛痘称作 variolae vaccinae，即「牛的痘」，以区别于天花。

items.en: Jenner published his inquiry into cowpox inoculation in 1798, and the cow-derived material became the model for protection.
items.cn: 詹纳于 1798 年发表关于牛痘接种的探究，这种取自牛的材料成了防病的范本。

items.en: The adjective vaccine, meaning of cowpox, turned into a noun for any preparation of this kind.
items.cn: 意为「牛痘的」的形容词 vaccine 转为名词，指任何这类制剂。

items.en: Laboratory methods replaced the cow as the source, but the name stayed for every trained-immunity product.
items.cn: 实验室方法取代了以牛为来源，但这个名字保留给了所有训练免疫的产品。

note.en: The look-alike group is the cow-derived family, while the near-meaning group gathers other ways of protecting a body from disease.
note.cn: 形近组是「牛」来源的词族；近义组收其他使人免于疾病的办法。

entries.definition: To give a vaccine to a person or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「给……接种疫苗」，由本词加动词后缀构成。

entries.definition: The act or result of giving a vaccine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疫苗接种」，由动词加名词后缀构成。

entries.definition: The cowpox virus, the original source material of vaccination.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指牛痘病毒，是疫苗接种最早的来源材料；同出「牛」词根。

entries.definition: The introduction of a weakened germ into the body, an older word often used for the same act.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接种」，指把减毒病原体引入体内，是较旧的说法。

entries.definition: The process of making the body immune, of which vaccination is one route.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「免疫」，指使身体获得免疫的过程，接种是其中一种途径。

entries.definition: An extra dose that strengthens the protection already given by a vaccine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加强针」，指增强既有免疫保护的一剂。

normalIntro.en: The hooks below use the cow root and the words that grew from it, not a made-up story.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子依据「牛」这个词根及其派生词，不用编造的故事。

normal.en: Vacca is Latin for cow, and the first vaccine material came from a cow.
normal.cn: vacca 是拉丁语的「母牛」，最早的疫苗材料就取自牛。

normal.en: Jenner used cowpox, variolae vaccinae, so the new practice took the cow name.
normal.cn: 詹纳用牛痘「variolae vaccinae」，新的做法因此得了「牛」的名字。

normal.en: Vaccine is the thing, vaccinate is the act, and vaccination is the process.
normal.cn: vaccine 是东西，vaccinate 是动作，vaccination 是过程。

normal.en: A flu vaccine is a seasonal dose, while a booster is an extra dose given later.
normal.cn: flu vaccine 是季节性的一剂；booster 是之后补打的加强一剂。

normal.en: Vaccine hesitancy names the delay or refusal of a vaccine even when it is offered.
normal.cn: vaccine hesitancy 指即使有疫苗也迟疑或拒绝接种。

abstract.en: Picture a vial of clear liquid that holds a harmless copy of a germ.
abstract.cn: 想象一小瓶清亮液体，里面装着无害化的病原体副本。

abstract.en: Picture a lab bench where the germ is grown, weakened and measured before it fills the vial.
abstract.cn: 想象实验台上病原体先被培养、减毒、计量，再灌进小瓶。

abstract.en: Picture a cold box carried from village to village until every arm has had its dose.
abstract.cn: 想象一只冷藏箱从一个村送到另一个村，直到每条胳膊都打过一针。

examples.en: The new vaccine was tested in twelve hospitals before approval.
examples.cn: 新疫苗在获批前于十二家医院接受了测试。

examples.en: Parents were asked to bring the child back for a second vaccine.
examples.cn: 家长被要求带孩子回来接种第二剂疫苗。

examples.en: Health workers carried the vaccine through flooded roads to reach the clinic.
examples.cn: 医护人员带着疫苗穿过被淹的道路抵达诊所。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瓦克辛」——听成「哇，克星」：疫苗一到，病就遇上克星；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 vacca（母牛）→ vaccinus（牛的）→ 医学拉丁语 variolae vaccinae（牛痘）→ 英语 vaccine（疫苗）。核心义是「取自牛身上的防病材料」，后来泛指一切训练免疫的制剂。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses run from the vial itself through the germ material and the delivery programme to a figurative safeguard against harmful ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项从小瓶本身，到瓶中的病原体材料，再到送针的接种行动，最后到抵御有害观念的比喻义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small vial of clear liquid holds a harmless copy of a germ.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小瓶清亮液体里装着一份无害化的病原体副本。

branches.en: THE VIAL: the dose itself teaches the body to resist one disease.
branches.cn: 小瓶线：这一剂本身教身体抵抗某一种病。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: at the bench the word names the grown and weakened germ.
branches.cn: 材料线：在实验台上，这个词指被培养、减毒的病原体。

branches.en: THE CAMPAIGN: when a whole population is dosed, the product names the programme.
branches.cn: 行动线：当全体人群都接种时，产品名就成了整个计划的名字。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: a small controlled dose of a harmful thing builds resistance to a larger one.
branches.cn: 比喻线：少量可控的有害接触，能对更大的威胁建立抵抗力。

branches.en: The vial and the campaign are the same protection seen at two scales.
branches.cn: 小瓶与接种行动是同一种保护在两个尺度上的样子。

intro.en: Vaccine is a Latin cow word that English turned into a medical family of verbs, nouns and adjectives.
intro.cn: vaccine 本是拉丁语中表示「牛」的词，英语把它扩展成由动词、名词、形容词组成的医学词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vacca and vaccinus are recorded words; variolae vaccinae is the eighteenth-century medical phrase built on them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vacca 与 vaccinus 都是有记录的词；variolae vaccinae 是十八世纪在这两个词基础上构成的医学术语。

items.example: Vacca is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: vacca 是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The adjective describes material taken from a cow.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述取自牛的材料。

items.example: The phrase named the disease that gave the practice its start.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语命名了促使这一做法开始的疾病。

items.example: Vaccinia names the virus used in the first vaccines.
items.exampleCN: vaccinia 指最早疫苗中使用的病毒。

items.example: English keeps the noun for the dose itself.
items.exampleCN: 英语用这个名词指那一剂本身。

items.example: The verb names the act of giving the dose.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指给人接种这一剂的动作。

items.meaning: the act or result of vaccinating
items.example: The noun of process grew from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 表示过程的名词由动词扩展而来。

items.example: The suffix forms vaccinate.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 vaccinate。

items.example: The suffix forms vaccination.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 vaccination。

definition_zh: 炎症；发炎；（旧）燃烧；（情绪的）激愤
definition_en: a condition in which a part of the body becomes red, hot, swollen and painful, especially as a reaction to injury or infection
core_image: 伤口边缘一圈发红发热的界线，像一小团被围住却仍在燃烧的火
scene: 换药时，护士发现切口周围又红又热，棉签一压病人就皱眉。The surgeon noted the inflammation around the wound and ordered a swab.
sceneCN: 这里 inflammation 是「炎症」（第 1 个义项：身体局部红、热、肿、痛的防御反应）；句意为外科医生注意到伤口周围的炎症，并开了拭子检查。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀回到动词，义为「使发炎；使燃烧；激怒」
由本词加形容词后缀 -atory 构成，义为「炎症的；煽动性的」
由 anti- 加本词构成，义为「抗炎的；消炎的」，也可作名词指消炎药
由本词同根构成，义为「易燃的；易激动的」，注意 in- 并不表示否定

senses.title: The body reaction to injury or infection
senses.titleCN: 炎症：身体对损伤或感染的反应
senses.definition: a local response of the body to injury or infection, marked by heat, redness, swelling and pain
senses.definitionCN: 身体对损伤或感染的局部反应，表现为热、红、肿、痛
senses.example: The redness and heat around the ankle were clear signs of inflammation.
senses.exampleCN: 脚踝周围的红与热是炎症的明显征象。
senses.why: Latin flamma is a flame, so inflammation is the body setting a small fire at the damaged spot to drive infection out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 flamma 是「火焰」，所以 inflammation 就是身体在受损处点起一小团火，把感染赶出去。

senses.title: An inflamed part or condition
senses.definition: a condition in which a particular organ, joint, or tissue is inflamed, often named as an illness
senses.definitionCN: 某一器官、关节或组织处于发炎状态的病症，常作为一个病名来说
senses.example: She was treated for an inflammation of the middle ear.
senses.exampleCN: 她因中耳发炎接受了治疗。
senses.why: Once the process settles in one place, the word can name that place as an illness.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个过程落在某个部位，这个词就可以把那个部位当作一种病来命名。

senses.title: The act of setting on fire
senses.definition: the act or state of burning, the older and literal sense of the Latin word
senses.definitionCN: 点燃或燃烧的状态，这是拉丁词更早、更字面的含义
senses.example: The old report describes the inflammation of the coal seam, which burned for years.
senses.exampleCN: 那份旧报告描述了煤层被点燃的情形，火烧了许多年。
senses.why: Inflammare means to set on fire, and English once used the noun for actual burning before medicine took it over.
senses.whyCN: inflammare 意为「点燃」，在医学占据这个词之前，英语曾用它指真正的燃烧。

senses.title: Passions set alight
senses.definition: a state of excited or angry feeling, especially in older writing about crowds or public opinion
senses.definitionCN: 激动或愤怒的情绪状态，多见于旧时描写人群或舆论的文字
senses.example: The speech produced an inflammation of public feeling that lasted for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 那场演讲激起了持续数周的公众激愤。
senses.why: The same flame image serves the emotions: a feeling is lit and spreads through a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 同一个火焰意象也可用于情绪：一种情绪被点燃，并在人群中蔓延。

intro.en: Inflammation goes back to the Latin verb for setting on fire, and medicine borrowed the flame for the heat of a damaged part.
intro.cn: inflammation 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「点燃」的动词，医学借这团火来形容受损部位的热。

items.en: Flamma means flame, and the verb flammare means to blaze or set alight.
items.cn: flamma 意为「火焰」，动词 flammare 意为「燃烧、点燃」。

items.en: Inflammare adds in- to the flame verb and means to set on fire or kindle.
items.cn: inflammare 在「火焰」动词前加 in-，意为「点燃、引燃」。

items.en: Inflammatio names a setting on fire, and medical writers used it for the heat and swelling of a diseased part.
items.cn: inflammatio 指「点燃」，医学作者用它来说患病部位的热与肿。

items.en: The four classical signs, heat, redness, swelling and pain, were already attached to the word by ancient physicians.
items.cn: 热、红、肿、痛这四个古典征象，古代医家已经系在这个词上。

items.en: English medical texts took the noun in the fifteenth century, and the literal fire sense faded into older writing.
items.cn: 英语医学文献在十五世纪采用这个名词，字面的「火」义退入旧式文字。

items.en: Modern medicine adds chronic and low-grade inflammation, where the fire burns slowly and quietly.
items.cn: 现代医学又添上慢性炎症与低度炎症，这时的火慢慢而无声地烧。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin flame family, while the near-meaning group gathers signs and neighbours of the same bodily reaction.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「火焰」词族；近义组收同一身体反应的征象与邻词。

entries.definition: To make a part of the body red and swollen, or to stir up strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使发炎、使红肿」，也指「激怒、煽动」；是本词的动词形式。

entries.definition: Relating to inflammation, or likely to provoke anger.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「炎症的」，也指「煽动性的」；由本词加形容词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Easily set on fire; the in- here does not mean not, so the word means the opposite of what its look suggests.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「易燃的、易激动的」；这里的 in- 不表示否定，词义与字形给人的印象相反，同根但不要与「不易燃」混淆。

entries.definition: An enlarged area of the body, one of the signs of inflammation rather than the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肿胀」，是炎症的征象之一，而不是整个过程本身。

entries.definition: The presence and growth of germs in the body, which often causes inflammation but is a different thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「感染」，指病原体在体内生长，常引起炎症，但二者不是一回事。

entries.definition: A mild soreness or annoyance, lighter and less specific than inflammation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「刺激、轻微发炎」，比炎症更轻、更不具体。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the flame root and the clinical signs that medicine actually attached to the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依据「火焰」词根，以及医学真正系在这个词上的临床征象。

normal.en: Flamma is flame, and in- puts the flame inside, so inflammation is a fire inside the body.
normal.cn: flamma 是火焰，in- 把火放到里面，所以 inflammation 就是身体里的一团火。

normal.en: The four old signs are heat, redness, swelling and pain, and all four follow the flame.
normal.cn: 四个古老征象是热、红、肿、痛，四者都跟着这团火走。

normal.en: Inflammatory is the adjective for the process, while an inflammatory speech is a figurative flame.
normal.cn: inflammatory 是这个过程对应的形容词，而 inflammatory speech 则是比喻性的火。

normal.en: Inflammable looks like it means not flammable, but it means easily set on fire.
normal.cn: inflammable 看起来像「不易燃」，实际意思是「易燃」。

normal.en: Anti-inflammatory drugs work against the heat, the swelling and the pain together.
normal.cn: anti-inflammatory 药物同时对付热、肿与痛。

abstract.en: Picture a small controlled fire ringing a cut, burning only what harms.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈受控的小火围着切口，只烧有害的东西。

abstract.en: Picture the same fire settling into one knee and giving that place a name.
abstract.cn: 想象同一团火落进一个膝盖里，让那个部位有了病名。

abstract.en: Picture an old oil lamp lit by hand: the flame is literal before it is medical.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏用手点亮的旧油灯：这团火先是字面的，后来才是医学的。

examples.en: Chronic inflammation is now treated as a risk factor for heart disease.
examples.cn: 慢性炎症现在被视为心脏病的风险因素。

examples.en: The cream reduces inflammation after a sunburn.
examples.cn: 这种药膏能减轻晒伤后的炎症。

examples.en: The doctor drained the abscess to relieve the inflammation.
examples.cn: 医生引流脓肿以缓解炎症。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因发炎」——读音像把「因」和「发炎」连起来：身上一发热发红，就是炎症；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 flamma（火焰）→ flammare（燃烧）→ inflammare（点燃，in- 表示「在内」）→ inflammatio（点燃；炎症）→ 英语 inflammation。核心义是「在体内点起的一小团火」，医学用它说红、热、肿、痛的反应。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses follow one flame: the body fire of inflammation, a single inflamed place, the literal burning of older English, and the figurative heat of public feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项跟着同一团火：身体的炎症之火、某一处的发炎、旧英语中字面的燃烧，以及公众情绪的比喻之火。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of red heat around a wound, like a small fire kept inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：伤口周围一圈红热，像一小团被围住而烧着的火。

branches.en: THE BODY FIRE: heat, redness, swelling and pain mark the damaged place.
branches.cn: 身体之火：热、红、肿、痛标记受损之处。

branches.en: ONE PLACE: when the fire settles in a joint or an ear, the place becomes an illness.
branches.cn: 一处之火：当火落在关节或耳朵里，那个部位就成了一种病。

branches.en: THE OLD FIRE: before medicine, the noun named actual burning.
branches.cn: 旧时之火：在医学之前，这个名词指真正的燃烧。

branches.en: THE INNER FIRE: anger and excitement are lit and spread like flame.
branches.cn: 内心之火：愤怒与激动被点燃，像火一样蔓延。

branches.en: Both the body and the feelings are described as something set alight.
branches.cn: 身体与情绪都被说成被点燃的东西。

intro.en: Inflammation is built from a Latin noun of flame; English adds verbs, adjectives and a negative-looking prefix to extend the family.
intro.cn: inflammation 由表示「火焰」的拉丁语名词构成；英语再加动词、形容词与一个看似否定的前缀来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin flamma, flammare, inflammare and inflammatio are all recorded; no form here is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flamma、flammare、inflammare 与 inflammatio 均有记录，这里没有重构形式。

items.example: Flamma is the picture behind the word.
items.exampleCN: flamma 是这个词背后的画面。

items.example: The verb turns the noun into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把名词变成动作。

items.example: The prefix puts the flame inside something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把火放到某物之内。

items.example: The compound verb gives the medical fire.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成动词给出医学上的那团火。

items.example: The noun of the process passed into English.
items.exampleCN: 表示过程的名词进入了英语。

items.example: English keeps the clinical sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了临床含义。

items.example: The short verb returns to the simple stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个短动词回到简单词干。

items.example: The suffix forms inflammation from the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由动词词干构成 inflammation。

items.example: The adjective extends the family to tone and speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把词族扩展到语气与言论。

items.example: The suffix forms inflammatory.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 inflammatory。

items.example: The adjective hides a trap for readers.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给读者埋了一个陷阱。

definition_en: a feeling of sickness in the stomach with an urge to vomit, or a strong feeling of disgust
core_image: 小船在灰浪里上下起伏，胃里也跟着一阵阵翻上来
scene: 渡轮刚驶出防波堤，浪头一个接一个打来，甲板上的人扶住栏杆。The nausea came in waves and did not leave until the boat reached calm water.
sceneCN: 这里 nausea 是「恶心、反胃」（第 1 个义项：胃里翻涌、想吐的感觉）；句意为恶心一阵阵袭来，直到船驶入平静水面才停。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ous 构成，义为「令人恶心的；感到恶心的」
由动词 nauseate 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人作呕的」
由本词加 -ate 构成，义为「使恶心；使厌恶」
由 nauseate 加 -ed 构成，义为「感到恶心的」

senses.title: A queasy stomach and the urge to vomit
senses.definition: the uncomfortable feeling that food might come up, often a warning sign of illness or poisoning
senses.definitionCN: 食物可能吐上来的不适感，常是疾病或中毒的预警
senses.example: The nausea began an hour after the medicine was taken.
senses.exampleCN: 服药一小时后开始恶心。
senses.why: Greek naus is a ship, and the first nausea was the sickness of people at sea.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 naus 是「船」，最早的 nausea 就是海上乘船之人的晕船。

senses.title: Sickness caused by motion
senses.definition: the specific sickness brought on by the motion of a ship, a car, or a plane
senses.definitionCN: 由船、车或飞机的晃动引起的特定不适
senses.example: Her nausea faded as soon as the ferry entered the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮一进港，她的晕船感就消退了。
senses.why: The word keeps its birthplace: the ship is the original cause of the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了出生地：船就是这种感觉最初的原因。

senses.title: Strong disgust
senses.definition: a feeling of deep distaste caused by something morally or physically repulsive
senses.definitionCN: 由道德或生理上令人反感的事物引起的深切嫌恶
senses.example: He looked at the forged documents with real nausea.
senses.exampleCN: 他带着真切的厌恶看着那些伪造的文件。
senses.why: A body that rejects bad food supplies the image for a mind that rejects a bad act.
senses.whyCN: 身体排斥坏食物的反应，为心灵排斥恶行提供了意象。

senses.title: In the phrase ad nauseam
senses.titleCN: 短语 ad nauseam：说到令人作呕
senses.definition: in the Latin phrase ad nauseam, meaning repeated until it makes the listener sick of hearing it
senses.definitionCN: 用于拉丁短语 ad nauseam，意为反复到令听者厌烦作呕
senses.example: The same excuse was repeated ad nauseam in every meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 同一个借口在每次会上都被反复说到令人厌烦。
senses.why: Latin ad nauseam means to the point of nausea, so endless repetition is pictured as a stomach that can take no more.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ad nauseam 意为「直到恶心为止」，无休止的重复被想象成再也装不下的胃。

intro.en: Nausea began as the Greek word for seasickness, and it still carries the ship inside it.
intro.cn: nausea 最初是希腊语中表示「晕船」的词，至今仍把那条船带在身上。

items.en: Naus means ship, and it also underlies Greek nautes, a sailor.
items.cn: naus 意为「船」，它也是希腊语 nautes「水手」的词根。

items.en: Nausia, built on the ship word, named the sickness of people at sea.
items.cn: nausia 由「船」这个词构成，指海上之人的晕船。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as nausea, keeping both the seasickness sense and the wider sense of stomach upset.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 nausea，既保留晕船义，也扩展为一般的胃部不适。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century, first for seasickness and then for any urge to vomit.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪采用这个词，先指晕船，后指任何想吐的感觉。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative disgust and the Latin phrase ad nauseam.
items.cn: 现代英语加上比喻性的厌恶，以及拉丁短语 ad nauseam。

note.en: The look-alike group is the family built on the same root, while the near-meaning group gathers related stomach feelings and words for disgust.
note.cn: 形近组是同一词根构成的词族；近义组收相关的胃部感受与表示厌恶的词。

entries.definition: Causing nausea, or, in loose modern use, feeling nausea.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人恶心的」，口语中也常用来表示「感到恶心的」；由本词加 -ous 构成。

entries.definition: Something that makes a person feel sick, physically or morally.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人作呕的」，可指生理上或道德上使人反感；由动词 nauseate 构成。

entries.definition: Feeling sick in the stomach, the form preferred for the person who feels it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「感到恶心的」，指人自身的感受，是较为规范的说法。

entries.definition: The general state of being ill, or vomiting, broader than nausea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疾病、呕吐」，比 nausea 更宽泛。

entries.definition: A mild uneasy feeling in the stomach, usually lighter than nausea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「反胃、轻微恶心」，通常比 nausea 轻。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of dislike, used mostly for moral or sensory revulsion rather than the stomach.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「厌恶、反感」，多指道德或感官上的反感，不强调胃部。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the Greek ship inside the word and the pairs English keeps around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依据词里那条希腊语的船，以及英语围绕它形成的搭配。

normal.en: Naus is ship, so nausea is the sickness a ship gives.
normal.cn: naus 是船，所以 nausea 就是船带来的不适。

normal.en: Naus also gives nautes, a sailor, and English nautical, everything about the sea.
normal.cn: naus 还给出 nautes「水手」与英语 nautical「航海的」，都与海有关。

normal.en: Nauseous describes what causes the feeling, while nauseated describes the person who feels it.
normal.cn: nauseous 描述引起这种感觉的东西，nauseated 描述感到恶心的人。

normal.en: Nausea and vomiting are written together in clinical notes as one pair of symptoms.
normal.cn: nausea and vomiting 在病历里常作为一个症状组合写在一起。

normal.en: Ad nauseam means repeated until the listener is sick of it.
normal.cn: ad nauseam 意为反复到听者厌烦作呕。

abstract.en: Picture a small boat rocking on grey water while the stomach rises and falls with it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小船在灰浪里摇晃，胃也随着一起一伏。

abstract.en: Picture the same boat entering the harbour and the rocking stops at once.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条船驶进港内，摇晃立刻停下。

abstract.en: Picture a face turning away from a cruel scene, the stomach reacting to what the eyes saw.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸从残酷的场景转开，胃对眼睛看到的东西起了反应。

examples.en: Nausea and a mild fever are common in the first days of the illness.
examples.cn: 发病头几天常见恶心与低热。

examples.en: She felt nausea on every bend of the mountain road.
examples.cn: 山路的每个转弯都让她恶心。

examples.en: The smell of the ward caused nausea among the visitors.
examples.cn: 病房的气味让探视者感到恶心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹灾」——读音近似，胃里闹了灾，翻江倒海：恶心、反胃；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 naus（船）→ nausia（晕船）→ 拉丁语 nausea（晕船；胃部不适）→ 英语 nausea。核心义是「船晃出来的那种翻胃感」，后来泛指恶心与厌恶。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses keep the ship at the centre: the queasy stomach, the motion that caused it, the disgust it images, and the Latin phrase for repetition to the point of sickness.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都绕着那条船：翻胃的恶心、引起它的晃动、由它取象的厌恶，以及表示「到恶心为止」的拉丁短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small boat rising and falling on grey water while the stomach rises with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：小船在灰浪里上下起伏，胃也跟着翻上来。

branches.en: THE STOMACH: the queasy feeling itself is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 胃部线：翻胃的感觉本身是日常义项。

branches.en: THE SHIP: motion is the original cause and still the sharpest image.
branches.cn: 船线：晃动是最初的成因，至今仍是最鲜明的意象。

branches.en: THE MIND: disgust borrows the stomach reaction for moral rejection.
branches.cn: 心理线：厌恶借用了胃的反应来表达道德上的排斥。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: ad nauseam marks repetition that has reached the stomach.
branches.cn: 短语线：ad nauseam 标出已经抵达胃部的重复。

branches.en: Both the body and the mind can be described as unable to take more.
branches.cn: 身体与心灵都可以被说成再也装不下了。

intro.en: Nausea is a Greek sea word that Latin and English kept almost unchanged, with English adding suffixes for the family.
intro.cn: nausea 是希腊语的「海」词，拉丁语与英语几乎原样保留，英语再加后缀扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek naus and nausia and Latin nausea are recorded forms; nauticus, the Latin source of nautical, shares the ship root.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 naus、nausia 与拉丁语 nausea 均有记录；拉丁语 nauticus 是 nautical 的来源，共享「船」这个词根。

items.example: Naus is the ship inside the word.
items.exampleCN: naus 是词里那条船。

items.example: The Greek noun names the sickness at sea.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词指海上的不适。

items.example: The same root names the person who works the ship.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根也命名在船上劳作的人。

items.example: Latin widened the sense beyond the sea.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把词义扩展到海以外。

items.example: English keeps the noun almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 英语几乎原样保留了这个名词。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: -ous 后缀构成这个形容词。

items.example: The verb names the effect on a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指对人的作用。

items.example: The suffix forms nauseous.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 nauseous。

items.example: The suffix forms nauseate.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 nauseate。

items.example: Nautical carries the same ship root into another family.
items.exampleCN: nautical 把同一个「船」词根带进另一个词族。
